problem_type: silent Electron exit when the profile is already owned
symptom: Launching the compiled desktop app while another Nomi instance is using the same profile exits with code 0 and no diagnostic, which is indistinguishable from an Electron or renderer startup failure.
direct_cause: The single-instance guard correctly relinquishes a second process, but the lock-conflict branch only called app.quit() and emitted no user-visible or terminal diagnostic.
class_root: Desktop startup had a fail-safe ownership rule without an observable failure contract, so development and packaged smoke runs could not distinguish profile contention from renderer failure.
affected_population: Developers launching pnpm start while the installed Nomi app is open
Packaged smoke or support workflows that reuse the default user profile
Users diagnosing a second launch that appears to do nothing
entry_points: Electron startup with a profile owned by another Nomi process
Single-instance handoff before the first BrowserWindow
internal_only_reason: The failure is entirely within Nomi's local Electron process ownership and startup diagnostics; no provider or external protocol can establish whether the local profile lock is held.
invariants: A process that does not own the profile lock still exits without registering UI, IPC, or capability writers.
Lock-conflict exit emits a stable diagnostic that identifies profile contention and gives an isolated-profile remediation.
MCP stdio and explicitly isolated E2E processes keep their existing non-conflicting startup behavior.
migration: No ownership semantics change. Existing single-instance behavior remains fail-closed; only the previously silent relinquish path gains an actionable diagnostic.
residual_risks: A renderer crash after the lock is acquired still requires the existing Electron console and crash-log diagnostics.
Launching pnpm start with a profile owned by a different application remains outside this contract.
